articles.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
articles.summary: When a vision-language model describes an image, it names one object at a time and it rarely repeats itself, yet how the model plans this order is far from obvious. We characterize the mechanism a VLM uses to decide where to look before it looks. The mechanism has four main parts. First, binding heads match the relevant text tokens against the image and resolve them into pointers to the matched image region. Second, the same binding heads bind each written answer to the region it came from, and the model turns it into a progress signal: a cursor, the position in the image up to which the list has been written. Third, a select step chooses the nearest unwritten region after the cursor, or stops. Finally, gaze heads execute the chosen pointer and return a concept of what is drawn there, which language heads and the late MLPs turn into a word in the language of the question. articles.title: Balanced Twin Weight Factorization for Efficient MLLMs
articles.summary: Weight Factorization (WF) methods aim to reduce a model's latency, memory, or both. These typically decompose a pretrained model into two or more factors that approximate the original model weights with fewer parameters and floating point operations (FLOPs). However, translating fewer FLOPs into reduced latency is challenging for WF methods in practice due to overhead introduced by replacing a single large weight matrix with multiple smaller ones. To address this, we propose Balanced Twin Weight Factorization (BTWF), which uses the unique structure of factorized models to simultaneously lower latency and increase learning capacity. Specifically, BTWF operates in the shared basis WF setting, where two or more layers are decomposed into a shared basis matrix and a layer-specific mixing matrix. articles.title: Hands-on ML Orchestration Tutorial with Airflow3 [P]
articles.summary: It's available in English and Spanish. A couple of months ago I was looking for a good ML orchestration tutorial, and I found Made With ML's orchestration lesson, part of its full MLOps tutorial. There were only two problems. First, it was written for Airflow 2, and from what I had gathered at the time, Airflow 3 has some differences. Second, my brain doesn't retain a tutorial I only read for long: I can read it and understand it, and it will soon be gone. So I was looking for something a bit more interactive. Since I couldn't find one (and since I had some tokens for Claude Fable 5.1), I decided to ask it to create an updated, interactive version. But the result needed WAY more work than I anticipated: reviewing and fixing it took much longer than I thought, but it's here now and I'm happy with it. It goes into detail and has actual exercises in some of the sections. Some other features are not in the original either. Hope it's useful to anyone looking to learn this. submitted by /u/T
